name: ActorDB
tagline: Erlang distributed SQL database that shards data into many small Raft-replicated SQLite 'actors'.
description: ActorDB, built by Biokoda, splits a database into many independent 'actors', each a full SQLite database stored on LMDB and replicated across nodes with Raft. Most queries hit a single actor (one user's mailbox or file tree, say) with full SQL and no global locks, while explicit multi-actor transactions and a sharded KV table type cover cross-cutting data. Clients connect over the MySQL wire protocol or Thrift, so ordinary MySQL drivers work. The design fits per-user data in apps like mail or file sync, but the project went quiet after release 0.10.29 in October 2019 and has had no commits since.
statusNote: No commits or releases since 0.10.29 (October 2019); effectively abandoned. Consider rqlite, dqlite or a distributed SQL database instead.

scale.notes: Scales by adding nodes and spreading many small actors across them; each actor is limited to what one SQLite database handles well.

strengths: Per-actor SQLite databases give full SQL with no global locks
Raft replication per actor provides strong consistency and automatic failover
MySQL protocol means existing drivers work unchanged
Nodes and schema changes can be added while the cluster is running
weaknesses: Abandoned since 2019; no security or compatibility updates
Data model must partition cleanly into actors to benefit
Cross-actor transactions are far slower than single-actor ones
Small community and sparse client libraries beyond MySQL drivers
useCases: Per-user data stores such as mail or file-sync backends (historically)
notIdealFor: Analytical queries that span the whole dataset
